tweet_pool.author: YounisJoseph
tweet_pool.text: This is a well-designed randomized control study that asks the question: Does an LLM's ability to diagnose and manage the same medical scenarios degrade when a patient is the communicator versus a physician. The result: 60% drop in diagnostic accuracy, 12% drop in appropriate
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Randomised controlled study with concrete quantified degradation figures.

tweet_pool.author: shanaka86
tweet_pool.text: 25 of 26 AI teams picked worse than random. Nature Biotechnology published the scores on 19th August 2026, and the gap runs 39 percent for random picking against 10 for the models across 511 blinded antibodies. Those came from 29 groups. Outside labs built and measured every one
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Peer-reviewed blinded benchmark result contradicting AI-for-biology claims.

tweet_pool.author: ProfBuehlerMIT
tweet_pool.text: Grok bots are incredible - and they can even manufacture real physical objects! Here is a little experiment I did last night: I created a team of bots and asked them to solve a complex engineering problem end to end - starting from four images as design cues, inferring
tweet_pool.selection_reason: MIT professor documenting a concrete multi-agent engineering-to-manufacture experiment.

tweet_pool.author: SteveMoraco
tweet_pool.text: I'm actually pretty upset Apple allowed this. While the feature is cool, the technical functionality that enables it is not cool. If I was Tim Apple, OAI would be temporarily banned from the App Store until this is reversed. I use iMessage because it is encrypted with server keys I can own. But now copies of my messages in what is supposed to be an encrypted-at-rest local cache can be fetched directly by ChatGPT and stored and processed in plain text on OpenAI/Microsoft servers.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Widely shared privacy objection to ChatGPT reading local iMessage caches on macOS; full text retrieved via thread lookup.

tweet_pool.author: undefinedKi
tweet_pool.text: Claude Code can now hack apps. AI agents that hack your own app, then hand you the exploit that worked. Strix is open source AI penetration testing. You give it a directory or a URL, it runs your app, finds the holes, and proves each one with a working exploit.

tweet_pool.author: davidsenra
tweet_pool.text: Sam Altman. OpenAI. August 23, 2026. Available everywhere you get podcasts.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Scheduled long-form Altman interview releasing today.

tweet_pool.author: antibearthesis
tweet_pool.text: ANTHROPIC VALUATION: $2T WALMART VALUATION: $825B ANTHROPIC REVENUE: $9B WALMART REVENUE: $735B BUT AI IS NOT A BUBBLE, RIGHT?
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Widely circulated valuation comparison framing the bubble debate with concrete figures.

tweet_pool.author: sairahul1
tweet_pool.text: Claude Code is eating your context window alive. Most people try to save tokens by writing shorter prompts. That's not where the real waste is. Your terminal output, repo context, MCP tools, logs, and Claude's own verbosity can burn 10-50x more tokens than necessary.
tweet_pool.selection_reason: Practical context-budget observation with a specific claimed magnitude.

tweet_pool.author: DN_degen
tweet_pool.text: Optimus just loaded a washing machine. Picking up clothes, handling them carefully, and putting them inside - all on its own. No teleoperation.

tweet_pool.author: ScarletKc_
tweet_pool.text: Why the hell not? What exactly did Chinese people do wrong? We just want to use GPT and Claude normally - why is it that even in Japan, even paying properly and using it normally, we still get banned? Just because we're Chinese?
tweet_pool.selection_reason: High-engagement account-access complaint that surfaced a broad nationality-based ban discussion.
